units.function: Unit tests for rejecting remote HTTP/MCP endpoints whose host resolves to private or reserved network addresses.
units.dependencyDirection: An untrusted URL flows into a service-level DNS guard with injectable lookup and error factory; resolved IP classification decides whether a later remote connection may proceed.
units.keyDataModels: URL hostname, DNS address/family list and stable remote_http_private_endpoint error code.
units.lifecycle: The guard resolves hostnames, rejects any private address, accepts an all-public result and directly rejects selected reserved IPv6 literals.
units.testAssessment: Tests cover private IPv4 resolution, all-public DNS and several reserved IPv6 ranges. Missing are localhost/link-local/multicast/IPv4-mapped IPv6 breadth, mixed answers, empty/failing DNS, schemes/ports/userinfo, redirects, DNS rebinding and TOCTOU, connection-time IP pinning, proxies, IDNA/trailing-dot normalization and validation on every reconnect.
units.designRationale: Reduce SSRF risk when user-configured remote tool endpoints are contacted by the server.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS data connectors and Agent tool gateways must not turn control-plane or execution nodes into paths toward cloud metadata, private enterprise services or forbidden egress destinations.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the stable error and resolve-all-addresses denial rule into the Data Connector/egress firewall. Enforce allowed scheme/port/domain policy, resolve and pin the actual connection address, revalidate redirects and reconnects, resist rebinding, support enterprise-approved private destinations explicitly and record policy evidence.
units.responsibilityConflict: A public-IP check alone does not prove that the destination or data export was authorized by the responsible human/data owner, and lookup-time approval may differ from connection-time routing.

units.function: Framework regression test proving the Express 5 named catch-all syntax dispatches shallow and deep Better Auth paths without matching unrelated API routes.
units.dependencyDirection: Express route syntax directly gates access to an external authentication handler; Supertest sends requests through an isolated in-memory app.
units.keyDataModels: HTTP method/path, named authPath wildcard, handler invocation count and status code.
units.lifecycle: All /api/auth subpaths reach the handler while unrelated /api paths remain 404.
units.testAssessment: A concise regression catches a real framework-upgrade failure. It does not exercise the production auth handler, middleware order, encoded paths, path normalization, CSRF/CORS, method policy, rate limiting or authentication outcomes.
units.designRationale: Pin a subtle Express 4-to-5 routing compatibility requirement that otherwise breaks every authentication endpoint silently.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs compatibility tests around IdentityPort HTTP adapters so framework upgrades cannot silently bypass or disable identity flows.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE the narrow upgrade-regression pattern only; Company OS identity contracts remain framework-neutral and require full adapter security tests.
units.responsibilityConflict: Route reachability proves neither identity assurance nor authorization, token audience, tenant isolation or audit responsibility.

units.function: Unit tests permitting replay of pending or approved OpenClaw Gateway Agent invitation acceptance and merging replacement gateway defaults before normalization.
units.dependencyDirection: Request type, vendor adapter type, existing join-request state and caller-supplied defaults flow through access-route helpers into a vendor-specific Agent configuration payload.
units.keyDataModels: Human/Agent request type, openclaw_gateway adapter type, join status, websocket URL, Paperclip API URL and arbitrary headers including x-openclaw-token.
units.lifecycle: Pending or already approved gateway Agent joins are replayable; rejected or human joins are not. Replay preserves old values, overlays a new API URL and gateway token, keeps unrelated headers and then rebuilds acceptance defaults.
units.testAssessment: Tests document state/type restrictions and merge precedence. Missing are immutable approved-payload digest, token secrecy/redaction/storage, endpoint validation, header allowlist, owner authorization, expiry, idempotency key, concurrency, rejected/revoked tokens and mandatory reapproval when any security-sensitive field changes.
units.designRationale: Allow an external gateway to retry onboarding and refresh connection material without duplicating a join request.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS Connectors need idempotent onboarding and credential rotation without changing the action a human approved.
units.companyOsFit: Reject this replay rule. Separate idempotent retry of an identical canonical payload from credential rotation; any endpoint, credential handle, permission or data-scope change creates a new versioned ConnectorBinding proposal and approval digest. Never carry raw vendor tokens in control-plane configuration.
units.responsibilityConflict: An approved request can be replayed with a different gateway token and Paperclip API URL while retaining approved status. Approval A can therefore activate connection B, and arbitrary old headers survive the merge. This violates exact action/digest binding and makes the responsibility record misleading.

units.function: HTTP integration tests proving invitation lookup and acceptance routes share an IP limiter, return Retry-After metadata and ignore spoofed X-Forwarded-For under the default untrusted-proxy setting.
units.dependencyDirection: Anonymous Express requests pass through access routes configured with a process-local limiter before stubbed database lookup and common error handling.
units.keyDataModels: Invite token URL, anonymous actor, socket IP, X-Forwarded-For, 429 response, Retry-After and structured retryAfterSeconds.
units.lifecycle: A first request reaches lookup and returns 404; the next lookup or accept request from the same socket is blocked for the remaining fixed window, regardless of spoofed forwarding headers.
units.testAssessment: Tests cover middleware ordering, shared budget across read/accept, response metadata and a useful proxy-spoof regression. Missing are trusted-proxy production configuration, distributed atomic counters, token/principal/device keys, IPv6 normalization, multi-process behavior, endpoint enumeration response parity, bounded state, telemetry and legitimate shared-NAT recovery.
units.designRationale: Protect both public invite surfaces before database work while avoiding client-controlled proxy headers in local/private deployment.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs consistent public-onboarding abuse controls across deployment profiles and ingress topologies.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE middleware ordering and shared endpoint budget; implement the production owner as an ingress-aware, shared, atomic limiter with explicit trusted-proxy policy, bounded retention, multi-signal keys and auditable overrides.
units.responsibilityConflict: The route identifies only a network source and does not establish a human principal. A local process counter supplies no durable responsibility evidence and may diverge across replicas.
